source_text: Can we bring Codex back in in a useful way?  Or do you think that the Zai agents are enough?

fragments.text: Can we bring Codex back in in a useful way?
Or do you think that the Zai agents are enough?

reply_acts.author: claude-4
reply_acts.text: (Codex) Yes, I think Codex is worth bringing back for work in the queue, not on the critical path. All three Zai seats are busy, and four independent jobs are waiting. codex-6 already knows two of them from its own discovery. My suggestion is to send codex-6 the `tuple`/`nomatch` fix now, and send codex-4 the `replaceM` export-alias fix.

reply_acts.author: claude-4
claude-4
reply_acts.text: (the capacity risk) Tonight's three Codex failures were "model at capacity". Two of them hit at start-up and cost seconds. One hit after 4 minutes and lost that discovery's work, but no code or merged state. So the cost of a failure is a re-dispatch, and I'd move a job to a Zai seat on the second failure. Your memory note says you run other Codex projects, so these jobs draw on usage they also need. That's the trade-off you'd be accepting.

reply_acts.author: claude-4
reply_acts.text: (go-ahead) Shall I send `tuple`/`nomatch` to codex-6 and the `replaceM` alias to codex-4?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (the chart) `progress.py` no longer shows a single "blocked" count. Each blocked row is now placed by where the fix for its blocker stands. 18 of 110 rows compile, and only 16 rows are blocked on something nobody is working on yet:

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (how a row is placed) Each blocking cause has an entry in a small table at the top of `progress.py`. The entry either names an agent currently working on that cause, or gives the commit that fixes it. The script asks git whether a row's probe ran before that fix commit. If it did, the row counts as "fixed, awaiting re-probe" rather than blocked.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (what "fixed, awaiting re-probe" means) Those 31 rows won't all compile on re-probe. Each will move to its next stop, which may be a new cause. A fix moves a row out of that stop, not necessarily all the way to compiled.
